newsitem.title: USA: "Empire Strikes Back" tops at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Empire Strikes Back" tops at U.S. box office.

text.p: Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader ruled the U.S. box office for the fourth consecutive weekend, but this time in a new movie -- the re-release of "The Empire Strikes Back," according to studio estimates released on Sunday.

The second movie in the "Star Wars" trilogy pulled in an estimated $22.4 million during the Friday to Sunday period, setting a new record for a February opener. The previous record was held by "Dante's Peak," which opened with $18.5 million two weeks ago.
"Empire" averaged $10,592 from 2,110 screens. Meanwhile, "Star Wars" slipped to second with $11.0 million after three weeks at the top.

Originally released in 1980, "The Empire Strikes Back" has now earned a total of $245 million at the U.S. box office. First time around, it opened on a Wednesday (May 21) on just 126 screens and earned $9.6 million in its first seven days.

The lifetime total for "Star Wars" rose to $438.7 million domestically, which includes $115.9 million from the reissue. This weekend, it averaged $5,000 after increasing its screen count by 96 to 2,200. Both movies are released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp.
"If 'Star Wars' wasn't in the marketplace, 'Empire' would have done more," said Tom Sherak, chairman of Fox's domestic film group, who said he was thrilled with the film's opening nonetheless.

The studio is considering delaying the scheduled March 7 re-release of the third part of the trilogy "Return of the Jedi" to give "Empire" three clear weeks at the box office, Sherak said. At present, "Jedi" would be competing with Howard Stern's "Private Parts," while March 14 offers Tim Allen's "Jungle2Jungle." Jim Carrey's "Liar, Liar" opens March 21.

The top 10 contained just one other new entry, the historical race drama "Rosewood" from director John Singleton. The movie opened in eighth with $3.2 million. Playing in 991 theaters, the movie averaged a reasonable $3,229. It is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner Inc.

Slipping one notch to third was the Clint Eastwood White House thriller "Absolute Power," which earned $9.0 million in its second weekend. Its 10-day total is $28.7 million. The movie was produced by Time Warner-owned Castle Rock Entertainment, and released by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp.

Also down one place each were "Dante's Peak" at fourth and "Vegas Vacation" at fifth. The former, a volcano drama, earned $7.0 million to take its three-week total to $45.4 million. "Vegas Vacation," a comedy starring Chevy Chase, earned $6.6 million, giving it a 10-day total of $21.4 million.
"Dante's Peak" is released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd. "Vegas Vacation" is released by Warner Bros.
